---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Productive Funded Organizational Investment
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(oiadp, xsga), 3), 1)), MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(xsga, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), xsga), 3), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Substantial organizational investment predicts stronger returns when it generates high operating income and is supported by enough net working capital to sustain the spending.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Requiring high SG&A intensity prevents firms with trivially small organizational spending from obtaining favorable productivity or runway ratios. The signal jointly tests investment scale, realized operating payoff, and financial fundability, resolving the ambiguity over whether SG&A is productive investment or overhead.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Comprehensive Operating Runway
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), ADD(xsga, ADD(dp, xint))), 3), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High operating margins are more durable when net working capital can support organizational spending, capital consumption, and financing costs.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The runway denominator aggregates three distinct recurring commitments rather than slightly modifying a familiar profitability numerator. Requiring a high margin separately prevents a large liquidity stock or unusually low commitments from identifying firms without meaningful operating strength.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Dual-Source Fixed-Charge Resilience
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(oibdp, ADD(dp, xint)), 3), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), ADD(dp, xint)), 3), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: High operating margins predict stronger returns when both operating earnings and net liquidity can independently cover depreciation and interest.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Earnings coverage measures current fixed-charge capacity, while liquidity runway measures the reserve available if operating conditions weaken. The margin leg controls small fixed-charge denominators, so the high end requires operating strength plus two distinct sources of financial resilience.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Flexible-Cost Comprehensive Runway
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 3)), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(MA(ABS(SUB(GROWTH(xsga, 1), GROWTH(sale, 1))), 3), 1))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), ADD(xsga, ADD(dp, xint))), 3), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: High margins are most durable when organizational costs scale with sales and liquidity can fund the firm's operating, capital-maintenance, and financing commitments.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Cost flexibility limits the rate at which commitments consume liquidity during an operating shock, giving the runway measure a direct economic role beyond static balance-sheet strength. The interaction identifies firms possessing both adaptable costs and sufficient reserves rather than substituting one archived financial-health leg for another.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Dual-Source Capital-Maintenance Resilience
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(oiadp, dp), 3), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), dp), 3), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: High after-depreciation operating returns are more valuable when both earnings and net liquidity provide substantial coverage of capital consumption.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The operating-return leg prevents small depreciation denominators from driving either coverage ratio. Requiring both profit-based and liquidity-based depreciation coverage targets firms able to maintain productive capacity from current earnings and accumulated financial reserves.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Fixed-Charge-Safe Organizational Runway
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(oibdp, ADD(dp, xint)), 3), 1)), MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(xsga, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), xsga), 3), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Organizational investment predicts stronger returns when it is financially fundable and operating earnings also cover depreciation and interest.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This distinguishes firms that merely spend heavily on SG&A from those with both the liquidity runway to sustain that investment and the earnings capacity to meet fixed charges. The interaction links organizational investment to two complementary financial constraints rather than treating SG&A intensity as unconditionally favorable.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE Productive Funded Organizational Investment---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Mechanically near-equivalent to the archived "Funded Organizational Runway" — since oiadp/xsga × xsga/sale = oiadp/sale, jointly requiring high ranks on the first two legs simply selects very-high-margin firms, leaving the identical xsga/sale and (act−lct)/xsga legs to do the work.

---CRITIQUE Comprehensive Operating Runway---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The runway denominator is dominated in magnitude by xsga for most firms, so this collapses to a two-leg version of the archived "Funded Organizational Runway"/"Fixed-Charge Liquidity Runway" pair rather than adding a distinct economic commitment.

---CRITIQUE Dual-Source Fixed-Charge Resilience---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is essentially the intersection of two already-tested archive signals ("Liquid Fixed-Charge Coverage" and "Fixed-Charge Liquidity Runway"), and its two coverage legs share the identical dp+xint denominator, so the added leg contributes little independent information.

---CRITIQUE Flexible-Cost Comprehensive Runway---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is the archived "Flexible-Cost Liquid Margin" with its financial-health leg swapped for another archived liquidity leg — precisely the cosmetic leg-substitution the reasoning claims to avoid.

---CRITIQUE Dual-Source Capital-Maintenance Resilience---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The cleanest and most internally consistent of the batch, with dp as a shared capital-maintenance yardstick for both earnings and liquidity, but it is still the same MIN(profitability, coverage, coverage) template as the archive's "Capital-Productive Liquid Earnings" and "Liquid Fixed-Charge Coverage" and its oiadp/at and oiadp/dp legs are highly correlated.

---CRITIQUE Fixed-Charge-Safe Organizational Runway---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: A direct recombination that takes the archived "Funded Organizational Runway" and replaces its margin leg with the archived oibdp/(dp+xint) coverage leg, offering no new economic mechanism beyond the existing components.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Liability-Neutral Intangible Cash Payback
EXPRESSION: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(oancf, DELTA(lct, 1)), 2), TS_SUM(ADD(xsga, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), 2)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms generating more cumulative operating cash, excluding current-liability financing, per unit of intangible-oriented spending earn stronger subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: This measures realized cash payback to SG&A and R&D rather than recombining operating margin, SG&A intensity, and liquidity-runway ranks. Subtracting current-liability growth prevents delayed payments from masquerading as investment payback, while treating unreported R&D as zero preserves an explicit reporting convention.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Capital-and-Debt-Efficient Profit Expansion
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(MA(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1), MAX(DELTA(RATIO(dp, at), 1), DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: High operating profitability is more durable when its improvement exceeds both growth in capital consumption and growth in debt burden.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: The quality leg compares operating improvement with the more adverse of capital-consumption expansion and debt expansion, so it does not mechanically reward deleveraging alone. Requiring a high profitability level separately filters weak firms that merely shrink their balance sheets.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Combined-Resource Fixed-Charge Coverage
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, SUB(act, lct)), ADD(dp, xint)), 3), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High operating margins predict stronger returns when the combination of current operating earnings and available net liquidity strongly covers depreciation and interest.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: The coverage ratio pools one-period operating capacity with the existing liquidity reserve, directly measuring total resources available against fixed charges rather than intersecting two coverage sorts with a shared denominator. The separate margin requirement prevents accumulated liquidity from compensating for weak operations.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Overhead-Shock Absorption Margin
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(SUB(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at), ABS(SUB(GROWTH(xsga, 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)))), 3), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High operating margins are more durable when the liquidity cushion is large relative to mismatches between SG&A growth and sales growth.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This integrates operating rigidity and financial capacity into a single stress-absorption measure instead of swapping one archived health leg for another. Firms receive a high quality score only when net liquidity is sufficient to offset the magnitude of their overhead adjustment mismatch.

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Cumulative Capital-Maintenance Capacity
EXPRESSION: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(TS_SUM(oiadp, 3), SUB(act, lct)), TS_SUM(dp, 3)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms whose cumulative after-depreciation operating income and current liquidity jointly cover cumulative capital consumption earn stronger subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: Combining multi-period earnings with the current liquidity reserve eliminates the highly correlated oiadp/at and oiadp/dp bottleneck legs. The cumulative denominator measures sustained capital consumption, reducing sensitivity to one unusually small depreciation observation.

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Residual-Liquidity Organizational Capacity
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, lct), ADD(dp, xint)), xsga), 3), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High operating margins are more valuable when liquidity remaining after reserving for depreciation and interest can still support organizational expenditure.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This imposes an explicit funding sequence: net liquidity first absorbs capital-consumption and financing commitments, and only the residual supports SG&A. It therefore tests discretionary organizational capacity after fixed charges rather than directly recombining archived SG&A, fixed-charge, and runway ranks.
